title: Preparation of Neutrally-charged, pH-responsive Polymeric Nanoparticles for Cytosolic siRNA Delivery
protocol: Dissolve polymer in 10 mM citric acid buffer (pH 4.0) at 3.33 mg/mL.
Pipette polymer solution to ensure thorough mixing and dissolution.
Mix polymer with ethanol if needed for initial dissolution, then dilute to desired concentration.
Add siRNA (50 μM in diH2O) to achieve an N+:P- ratio of 10.
Incubate the mixed polymer and siRNA solutions for 30 minutes.
Add a 5-fold excess of 10 mM phosphate buffer (pH 8.0) to the solution.
Mix gently by pipetting or inverting the tube after adding the phosphate buffer.
Pipette 10 μL of the final si-NP solution onto pH test strips.
Confirm that the final pH is neutral (~7.2-7.5).
Record the size and surface charge of resulting si-NPs using dynamic light scattering (DLS).
Filter 1 mL of si-NPs (0.1 – 1.0 mg/mL) through 0.45 μm pore-size syringe filters into a square quartz or polystyrene cuvette.
Measure size and surface charge using a DLS instrument according to the manufacturer’s specifications.
Confirm the size and morphology of si-NPs by imaging analysis using transmission electron microscopy (TEM).
Add 5 μL of si-NP solution at 1 mg/mL to TEM grids.
Incubate for 60 s.
Blot dry for 3 s.
Add 5 μL of 3% uranyl acetate solution and incubate for 20 s.
Blot dry for 3 s.
Dry grids overnight under desiccation.
Image grids according to the protocol established for the specific microscope to be used.
Characterize the loading of siRNA in si-NPs at various N+:P- ratios using agarose gel retardation.
Produce a 2% agarose gel by adding 2 g of electrophoresis grade agarose powder to 100 mL of 1x TAE buffer at pH 8.0.
Heat uncovered until all agarose is dissolved (1-3 min).
Cool the agarose solution, then add 5 μL of ethidium bromide (10 mg/mL in H2O), and mix well.
Pour agarose into a gel tray and place comb to produce wells.
Let dry for 30 min.
Carefully remove comb to leave behind loading wells.
Fill the gel tray to the max fill line with 1x TAE buffer.
Generate si-NPs according to the procedure for various N+:P- ratios.
Place 2 μL aliquots of loading dye on paraffin film for each si-NP formulation.
Mix 10 μL of si-NP solution with loading dye on paraffin film by pipette.
Add si-NP/loading dye solutions to agarose gel wells.
Run voltage source at 100 V for 35 min (or until samples have traversed 80% of gel length).
Visualize siRNA bands on a UV transilluminator according to the manufacturer’s specifications.
Generate luciferase si-NPs using luciferase siRNA and scrambled si-NPs using a scrambled siRNA sequence as control.
Formulate both si-NPs at the same final N+:P- ratio and at the optimum ratio identified by agarose gel retardation studies.
Seed luciferase-expressing cells in 96-well black-walled plates at a density of 2,000 cells per well.
Allow cells to adhere overnight in full media (DMEM, 10% FBS) in an incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2, 95% humidity).
Dilute si-NPs into full serum media for a final volume of 100 μL per well and siRNA concentration of 100 nM.
Treat cells for 24 h with si-NPs.
Remove treatments after 24 hours.
Replace the media with full serum media containing 150 μg/mL D-luciferin.
Incubate cells for 5 minutes.
Measure luminescence on a plate reader or in vivo optical imaging system according to manufacturer’s specifications.
Replace luciferin-containing media with fresh, full serum media.
Incubate cells for 24 hours more.
Remove media and replace with full serum media containing 150 μg/mL D-luciferin after 48 hours total treatment time.
Incubate cells for 5 minutes before measuring luminescence at the 48-hour timepoint.
Maintain cells under sterile conditions while measuring luminescence for longitudinal studies.
